questions.question: Explain the use of extreme long shot in the context of TV.
questions.solution_html:
• Extreme Long Shot (ELS): The camera is at the farthest distance from the subject - ESL
  • emphasises background and spatial scale - invariably used at the beginning of scenes to
  • set the stage with sweeping views (e.g., city skyline, farm, beach).
questions.final_answer: set the stage with sweeping views (e.g., city skyline, farm, beach)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is meant by “conversational, visual-driven” language in TV news?
questions.solution_html:
• TV scripts are written to be heard - Sentences must be short, clear, without jargon
  • complex vocabulary, or long explanations - Conversational. Television news is fast paced
  • emotionally engaging and visual. News in TV is not just about telling the story –
  • it is about showing the story - visual-driven.
questions.final_answer: it is about showing the story - visual-driven
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: / the passage. Which theory do you find most relevant in today’s digital media environment, and why?
questions.solution_html:
• 1. The Medium, Not the Message (Marshall McLuhan) electronic media exert a
  • profound influence on human behaviour, not through the messages they convey, but
  • through the sensory environment they create. 2. Reinforcement Theory (Joseph
  • Klapper) mass media primarily reinforces existing beliefs, values and social norms rather
  • than introducing significant change. 3. Narcotising Dysfunction (Lazarsfeld and
  • Merton) Exposure to a constant stream of information result in superficial awareness
  • without corresponding engagement.4. Catharsis Theory (Seymour Feshbach) media
  • serve as a psychological outlet, allowing individuals to purge aggressive/ antisocial
  • emotions through vicarious experiences. 5. Media as Windows on the World (Edward
  • Shils and David M White) democratise access to cultural content by making more of the
  • good accessible to more people. 6. Corruptive Effects (Fredric Wertham) media content
  • fosters materialism, antisocial behaviour and emotional desensitisation causing damage
  • to moral and social development.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyse the different types of news. / Explain the differences between human visual perception and camera
questions.solution_html:
• Types of news 1.Direct/Straight news is a straight forward account of a happening. It
  • usually answers five Ws (what, when, where, who, why) and one H (how). These five
  • Ws and one H are known as news elements. Three key parts of a news story are the
  • headline, the lead and remainder. 2. Feature - It goes beyond a direct news story. It
  • explores the background, probes in depth an idea or event.
questions.final_answer: explores the background, probes in depth an idea or event
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
